summary.headline: Sigma Advanced Systems Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 12% QoQ to INR417 crores, with operational EBITDA of INR82.28 crores (19.7% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR417 crores in Q2 FY27, up from INR374 crores in Q1, and operational EBITDA rose to INR82.28 crores from INR61 crores at a 19.7% margin. Profit after tax excluding associate share was INR48.6 crores versus INR35.41 crores in Q1. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crores at about 20% EBITDA margin, and said the UK operations and Sri City facility are moving work to India to lift margins. Management also announced a planned fundraise of up to INR3,000 crores to fund acquisitions, with closings targeted for Q4.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR374 crores in Q1 (about 11-13% QoQ)

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax (excl. associate share of profit/loss)
H1 FY27 revenue (as cited in Q&A)

financial_highlights.value: about INR80 crores (term loan INR76 crores)
financial_highlights.change: increase in H1 noted by analyst

segments.name: UK aerospace (Nasmyth, Bromford)
segments.commentary: Management said UK EBITDA margin improved at least 200 bps per quarter from Q3 FY26 to Q2 FY27 after about GBP 8-9 million of investment in equipment, buffer stock and supply chain. On-time-in-full delivery rose from 65% to about 97%. Aerospace capacity utilisation in India is about 15%.

segments.name: Defence exports (artillery ammunition)
segments.commentary: Defence export order book is about INR2,700 crores. About 85% of the 40,000-unit M107 export order revenue was recognised in Q1-Q2, with the balance completing in October and reflecting in Q3. Shell manufacturing is being insourced at Sri City, with only forging outsourced.

segments.name: Domestic defence and homeland security
segments.commentary: Domestic defence is about 3-4% of the mix, per analyst. Management cited a large BSF counter-drone contract under MHA and Government of India orders for Indrajal Ranger. Electronics run on a single shift.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of close to INR1,900-2,000 crores at about 20% EBITDA margin.
EBITDA margin improvement of 200-400 bps by end of FY27 and a further 400-600 bps by end of FY28, from transferring manufacturing to India.
Sri City facility to reach 50-60% capacity utilisation by end of FY28 and full utilisation by FY29, per management.
Aerospace EBITDA margin targeted at 25-30% in FY28, with UK fixed base retained (about 30% of UK-related work stays in UK, 70% moves to India).
UK execution expected to grow 15-20% YoY; new facility expected to ramp about 15% per quarter.
Fundraise of up to INR3,000 crores, with acquisition closings expected in Q4 FY27 (targets USD100-150 million in size).
capex_capacity: Sri City facility commenced production in September 2026 and has started shipping parts to the UK.
Management said no further capex is needed for the next few years; capacity is in place and there is no capacity constraint across manufacturing facilities.
Capacity utilisation: aerospace about 15% in India, ammunition about 20%, defence electronics on a single shift.
CCT (control/CCF related) utilisation 10-15% currently, expected to rise about 10% per quarter, per management.
Investment in palletisation and automation at UK operations to enable 24/7 running of certain machines.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR10,000 crores plus, 90% international; defence exports order book about INR2,700 crores.
New orders announced from July 1 to date total INR3,915 crores; much of this expected to convert in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Management said NATO allied ammunition demand and counter-drone demand support the medium-term order outlook; repeat orders are linked to delivery milestones.
UK aerospace order book described as executable and long-term (5-7 years visibility), with backfill commitments contracted for transferred work.
Revenue is about 90% export-driven (GBP, USD, EUR) and about 10% domestic; direct customer relationships with OEMs and primes, no sub-tier sales.

qa_highlights.question: What has been invested in Nasmyth and Bromford post-acquisition, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About GBP 8-9 million invested across working capital, buffer stock, supply chain and new equipment, lifting OTIF from 65% to about 97%. Insourcing and new kit are expected to continue the quarterly margin improvement over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose and timing of the INR3,000 crore fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily to fund acquisitions; management expects transactions to close around Q4, subject to shareholder approval. Management said no working capital raise is needed given cash and working capital lines.

qa_highlights.question: How is the M107 export order accounted for and is the 155mm fuse order a standalone order?
qa_highlights.answer: About 85% of the 40,000-unit M107 order revenue was recognised in Q1 and Q2, with the remaining 15% completing in October and reflecting in Q3. Fuse and shell orders are separate component orders that together form an ammunition solution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MIL CCF arrangement and time to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: An exclusive MOU with Munitions India Limited, bringing European partner technology already battle-proven and indigenised in India. Management expects supply to MIL within 6-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from H1 revenue of about INR800 crores to the INR2,000 crore FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected from aerospace and defence exports, with domestic defence skewed to Q3-Q4. Management cited INR3,915 crores of new orders since July 1, many executing in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debt position and repayment planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR80 crores, mostly working capital; term loan of INR76 crores with repayment strategy not finalised. Other term borrowings follow a schedule running January 1 to December 31, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the acquisition size and target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are businesses with about USD100-150 million revenue, EBITDA positive, with OEM customer access and capacity to transfer work to India. Management said it avoids loss-making companies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is aerospace EBITDA lower and what margin is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low UK margins to a large capital and overhead base and says automation and India transfer will lift margins. FY28 aerospace margin target is 25-30%, while keeping a UK base of about 500-plus employees.

risks_watch: Execution of the 15% to 20% UK growth and India transfer, including whether the 30:70 UK-India work split holds and margins converge toward FY28 targets.
Closing and integration of acquisitions targeted for Q4 FY27, and use of the up-to-INR3,000 crore raise; shareholder approval pending.
Q3-Q4 revenue ramp needed to reach the INR1,900-2,000 crore FY27 guidance from H1 of about INR800 crores.
Dependence on export defence orders, NATO demand and repeat-order milestones; M107 margin and insourcing progress.
Limited disclosure: management declined to give customer-wise order book split and FY28 forward numbers beyond one to two quarters.
Debt repayment strategy for the INR76 crore term loan and classification of bank deposits in the cash flow statement.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on order momentum, margin trajectory and the M&A pipeline, with specific targets given. Less forthcoming on customer breakdowns, FY28 numbers, acquisition identities and the debt repayment plan, where answers were brief or deferred.
key_quotes: What made the quarter exceptional was the new order wins from our acquisition, which consolidates our leading position in aerospace and wings.
We're in a very unique position, being an Indian player focused on exports.
So there is no gap between the order book and what we're currently executing.
We are not looking at any companies that will put a drag on our P&L.

adds.what: Sri City facility (production commenced Sept 2026, shipping parts to UK)
UK palletisation and automation investment enabling 24/7 running of certain machines

growth.why: Management targets FY27 revenue of about INR1,900-2,000 crore (vs H1 about INR800 crore, implying steep H2 ramp) at ~20% EBITDA margin, backed by a ~INR10,000 crore order book, INR3,915 crore new orders since July 1 and Sri City capacity commissioned Sept 2026; delivery specifics are partial, with aerospace India utilisation only ~15%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: by end FY27; further by end FY28
rows.why: Management targets 200-400 bps EBITDA margin gain by end FY27 and a further 400-600 bps by end FY28 from India transfer; operational EBITDA margin already rose to 19.7% in Q2 from about 16.3% in Q1 (INR61 crore on INR374 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sri City facility commenced production in September 2026 and has started shipping parts to the UK, with utilisation targeted at 50-60% by end FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue of about INR800 crore must roughly double in H2 to reach the INR1,900-2,000 crore FY27 target, backed by INR3,915 crore of new orders since July 1; UK execution guided to grow 15-20% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no further capex is needed for the next few years and there is no capacity constraint, with aerospace India utilisation at about 15% and ammunition at about 20%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated rather than raised FY27 guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crore, and the H2 ramp required is steep relative to H1 of about INR800 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 target needs H2 revenue of roughly INR1,100-1,200 crore versus about INR800 crore in H1, and the M107 order is 85% recognised with the balance in Q3; UK margin and India transfer execution are unproven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: An exclusive MOU with Munitions India Limited for European partner technology expects supply within 6-18 months, but no product launch date was firmly set.

rows.label: INR3,915 crore new orders since July 1 converting in Q3-Q4
rows.why: Much of the INR3,915 crore of new orders is expected to convert in Q3-Q4 FY27, against an order book of about INR10,000 crore plus with 90% international.

rows.label: Up to INR3,000 crore fundraise for acquisitions
rows.why: Management expects acquisition closings around Q4 FY27 subject to shareholder approval, with targets of USD100-150 million revenue, EBITDA positive.

rows.label: UK automation and palletisation for 24/7 running
rows.why: UK margin rose at least 200 bps per quarter from Q3 FY26 to Q2 FY27 after GBP 8-9 million invested, and OTIF rose from 65% to about 97%; further insourcing expected to continue the quarterly margin gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on order momentum, the 200-400 bps margin path and the M&A pipeline, but deferred on customer splits, FY28 numbers and the debt repayment plan; analysts pushed on the steep H2 ramp needed for INR1,900-2,000 crore and on the debt rise.
